description: Create AI lifestyle product photos from one plain image. Place the item in a room, table or cafe scene so shoppers picture using it without a shoot.

steps_h2: How to use the AI product scene generator
steps_lead: Upload the product, name the place, and download a square scene.

steps.d: Use one photo with the whole item in frame. Shape and small details should be easy to see.
Try a room, a table, or a market. Name the surface and one prop so the scene supports the product.
Check the scene against your plain photo, then download the square image for the store or an ad.

faq.q: What are AI lifestyle product photos?
faq.a: They place your real product photo in a room, on a table, or in another everyday setting. You still review the result before you publish.

faq.q: How do I make a lifestyle product photo?
faq.a: Upload one product photo, choose or describe the setting, and download a square image. The credit cost appears before the job starts.

faq.q: Can I use the scene on a product page?
faq.a: Yes. Pair it with a plain product photo when shoppers also need an exact view of the item. Downloads have no watermark and are licensed for commercial use.
Yes. Pick a room, a cafe, or a market moment, or describe the surface and light you want.

faq.q: Can I change the scene after the first result?
faq.a: Yes. Start again with a different surface or prop. Each photo costs 24 credits.

faq.q: Does the scene replace my plain product image?
faq.a: No. Keep the original photo for details. Use the scene when you want shoppers to picture where the item belongs.

faq.q: Can I post the scene in a social ad?
faq.a: Yes. Finish the headline and the offer in your ad editor. The photo does not include your price.

faq.q: How is this different from a photoshoot?
faq.a: A shoot needs a place, props, and time on a calendar. Here you start from a photo you already have. Read [how to take product photos for AI](page:guide-product-photo-tips) if the source image is hard to read.

faq.q: Can I use the scene on a Shopify store?
faq.a: Yes. Download the square image and upload it on the product page yourself. Each photo is 24 credits, shown before you start.

faq.q: Can I post the scene on Instagram?
faq.a: Yes. These square images work as Instagram product scene photos. Add the caption in Instagram, and add any price in your own editor.

faq.q: Can I add text, a logo, or run many photos?
faq.a: Yes. Add a short line of text or your logo on the scene, or edit a set of photos together. You can also connect an API so the store requests new scenes. Each photo is 24 credits, shown before it starts. There is no free plan.

platforms.h2: Your full set of product image tools
platforms.lead: Create, edit, and prepare product photos for the store, a marketplace, and ads, from one picture or a whole catalog.

items.d: Take the old backdrop off and put a clean studio setting behind the item.
Describe a color or a surface while the product stays recognizable from the photo you uploaded.
Put the item on a table, on a shelf, or in a hand so shoppers see daily use. That is the scene this page makes.
Lift the light, clear a stray object, and size the photo for a store page or an ad.
Place clothing or an accessory on an AI model so shoppers can judge the fit.
Download a square photo with no watermark and use it on the site, a marketplace, or an ad. You add the price yourself.
Even out light, detail, and color on the photo you already have before the scene goes up.
Reframe a tall shot into a wider one, or the other way, when a channel wants a different shape.
Connect an API to the store or marketplace so a new scene can be requested from the catalog. Each photo is still 24 credits, shown first.
Place a short offer or the product name on the finished scene. The price still comes from you, not from the photo.
Apply one backdrop or one size to a set of photos together, instead of opening them one by one.
Hand a scene to a teammate for a look before it goes on the product page.
Save the logo, the type, and the colors you reuse so the next scene stays recognizably yours.
Draft a simple logo when the shop does not have one yet, then place it on later photos.
Open the same photos from a phone or a computer and keep going.
